grh_8636c655b5827ce4c1c9.title: Trooper Lopez
paragraphs: After a Butterfield stage is ambushed near Fort Bowie, survivor Lopez warns the Army that outlaw Joshua Lucas is operating in the territory. Sergeant Major Michael Hawks initially distrusts him, but the larger danger emerges when Lucas targets two new Gatling guns being moved secretly in a medicine-show wagon. Lopez proves his loyalty as the soldiers work to keep the weapons from being used in an ambush against their own troops. In the final attack the Army avoids Lucas's trap, defeats the gang, and takes Lucas, but Lopez is mortally wounded. As he dies, the men who doubted him acknowledge him as a trusted friend and brother.

[[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Don Diamond, Keith Andes, Len Birman, Steven Markle, and Ted Brown. grh_86d108ed966f22d03e3b.title: Condition Red
paragraphs: A documentary-style adaptation of Captain Frederick J. Bell's Condition Red uses the destroyer he calls the G to explain life and combat aboard a U.S. Navy destroyer in the South Pacific. It moves from a Japanese air attack to damage control, anti-submarine tactics, the responsibilities expected of junior officers, cramped living conditions and the ship's constant readiness for another alarm. Rather than one continuous plot, the broadcast combines action scenes with Bell's descriptions of destroyer crews, training, endurance and the peculiar pride sailors develop in an uncomfortable but hard-hitting ship.

This [[show|words-at-war|Words at War]] broadcast aired on January 25, 1944. [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Jack Lloyd, Alan Bunce, Jerry Macy, and Geoffrey Bryant. Other credited names include Anton M. Leader as director, Gerald Holland as radio adaptor, and Jack Costello as host.
The surviving recording runs about 29 minutes.
This version dramatizes [[work|work.words.2ac13b64ab1a7336|Condition Red]]. Frederick Bell is credited as author and Gerald Holland adapted it for radio.

grh_8690925c37711e6692f0.title: Mysterious Hemophilia Patient
paragraphs: A secret patient admitted as John Smith proves to be Philip III, the former king of Corsonia who abdicated fifteen years earlier to make his country a democracy and has returned in disguise before a crucial plebiscite. Kildare and Gillespie find an operable cancerous growth obstructing his pylorus, but Philip is also a hemophiliac and may bleed to death if they operate; with only about two months to live otherwise, he accepts the extreme risk. After intensive preparation, rapid surgery and repeated transfusions he survives, the democratic side wins the Corsonian vote, Sarvo becomes president, and Philip is later appointed ambassador to the United States.

This [[show|dr-kildare|Dr. Kildare]] broadcast aired on May 18, 1951. The cast includes Lionel Barrymore, Lew Ayres, [[person|virginia-gregg|Virginia Gregg]], Ted Osborne, and Lawrence Dobkin. Other credited names include Joe Bigelow as director, Raymond Katz as producer, Joel Murcott as writer, and Dick Joy as announcer.
